conventions.datetime_et: ISO 8601 with the America/New_York offset; the clock is the source's own
conventions.release_date_nominal: the date the release WOULD fall on under the source's own standard rule: EMPSIT the first Friday of the month, EIA the standard weekday, FOMC the meeting's last day. A DESCRIPTOR computed from the sourced date, never a source of one. Empty for CPI, which has no day rule.
conventions.holiday_shift: the sourced date differs from release_date_nominal. For EIA it is exactly the page's own holiday exception table; for EMPSIT it also covers the 2019 and 2025 funding lapses, which are named in partial_or_disrupted_years.
conventions.method: fetched = off the live official page; archived = off a Wayback capture of that same official URL, which is the source_url. 'inferred' is REFUSED by the builder.
conventions.eia_rows_without_an_exception: EIA publishes a standard sentence plus an exception table, not a list of weeks. A normal week's date and time come from the standard sentence parsed off the governing page for that year and that page's table not listing the week. Unannounced delays are not visible to any published schedule.

G1.rule: every row carries a source_url and a method in {fetched, archived}

G3.rule: CPI/EMPSIT on weekdays; EMPSIT on a Friday unless holiday_shift; FOMC statement on the meeting's last day

G4.rule: for 2016-2024 the CPI, EMPSIT and FOMC date sets equal data/macro_release_calendar.json, or every difference is listed

G5.rule: 08:30 ET -> 13:30 UTC in January, 12:30 UTC in July

fomc_unscheduled_meetings_without_a_same.consequence: the CSV row is the statement, not the meeting; no clock was ever published for the meeting day, so no row is written for it

EIA_WPSR.standard: 10:30 ET on Wednesdays, read from the page's own sentence
